author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Police in Jackson, Mississippi, say additional arrests are expected in the homicide investigation of Tasia Fortune, a 29-year-old mother of four who was found hanging from a tree behind an abandoned home on August 3. The state medical examiner ruled the death a homicide, shifting the case from an unexplained death inquiry to an active criminal investigation.

Authorities arrested 51-year-old Jarques Ratliff on warrants connected to Fortune’s death. Police have not publicly described Ratliff’s relationship with Fortune or provided a suspected motive. Investigators also have not detailed what evidence led to the homicide finding, saying the inquiry is continuing.

Fortune’s family has pressed for answers since her death and welcomed the arrest while emphasizing that key questions remain. Relatives described her as resilient and said she had been working to rebuild her life after periods of homelessness and domestic abuse. The announcement that more arrests are anticipated makes the case an active developing story; police are asking that conclusions about responsibility wait for verified findings and court proceedings.
dek: One man has been arrested after the medical examiner ruled the 29-year-old mother’s August death a homicide.
headline: Mississippi police expect more arrests in Tasia Fortune homicide
